# AGent Energy Closes $11M Series Seed Round to Unlock 200 GW of Behind-the-Meter Power

* by [Sepehr Achard](https://igrownews.com/author/sepehrachard/)
* 14th August 2026

## Key Takeaways

* AGent Energy closed an $11 million Series Seed round co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures, bringing its total funding to $17 million within 12 months of the company’s founding.
* Intrepid Investment Management joined the round as a new investor, alongside existing backers CIV and Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP).
* AGent Energy’s AI-based platform aggregates and dispatches distributed generation at commercial, industrial, and institutional sites, targeting more than 200 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity.
* The company currently dispatches generation in three North American wholesale power markets: PJM, MISO, and ERCOT.
* Stephen Wemple of Spero Ventures joins AGent Energy’s board of directors, and Aram Ouligian of MassMutual Ventures joins as a board observer.

## AGent Energy Raises $11 Million Series Seed Round

AGent Energy, an AI-driven distributed power plant developer in the behind-the-meter [renewable energy](https://igrownews.com/renewable-energy-news/) market, has closed an $11 million Series Seed financing round co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures.
The round brings the company’s total funding to $17 million within 12 months of its founding.

Intrepid Investment Management joined the round as a new investor, alongside existing backers CIV and Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP), which had provided AGent Energy’s earlier funding.

## Investors Back AGent Energy’s Growth

“Closing $17 million in our first year reflects both the urgency of the grid reliability challenge and the speed at which our team executes,” said [Stephanie Hendricks](https://www.linkedin.com/in/stephanie-hendricks-85b56613/) , CEO and co-founder of AGent Energy.

“The grid doesn’t need to wait five years for new steel in the ground. The capacity is already there, and AGent has built the intelligence layer to unlock it,” said [Stephen Wemple](https://www.linkedin.com/in/stephen-wemple-a9168a64/) of Spero Ventures.

AGent Energy Raises $11M Seed

AGent Energy, a Houston-based developer of AI-driven distributed power plants, has announced the closing of an $11 million Series Seed financing round. This new capital brings the company's total funding to $17 million in its first 12 months of operation.

## Investors

The round was co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures. Additional participating investors include Intrepid Investment Management, as well as existing investors Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP) and CIV.

## AGent Energy Use of Funds

AGent Energy plans to use the new capital to aggressively scale its team and accelerate its push to unlock over 200 GW of behind-the-meter generation across commercial and industrial facilities, as well as the municipal, university, school, and hospital sectors.

## About AGent Energy
Founded in 2025, AGent Energy is led by CEO and co-founder Stephanie Hendricks. The company utilizes an AI-based technology platform to aggregate, orchestrate, and monetize distributed generation resources in power markets, providing grid reliability and economic benefits for large energy users and grid operators.

# AGent Energy Closes Series Seed to Unlock 200+ GW of Behind-the-Meter Generation Across Commercial, Industrial, and Institutional Sectors

Posted on August 13th, 2026 | Filed under [Press Releases](https://www.miningstockeducation.com/category/press-releases/)

_Round Co-Led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures with Participation from Intrepid Investment Management and Existing Investors Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP) and CIV; Brings Total Funding to $17 Million in Just 12 Months, Making It One of the Fastest-Funded Distributed Energy Resource Companies to Date_

HOUSTON , Aug.
13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — AGent Energy, a trailblazing developer of AI-driven distributed power plants, today announced it has closed an $11 million Series Seed financing co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures, with participation from Intrepid Investment Management and existing investors CIV and Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP). The round follows a $6 million financing from CIV and ZIP, which closed within two months of founding, bringing AGent’s total funding to $17 million in its first 12 months. It’s a striking vote of confidence in behind-the-meter generation as the next great frontier of U.S. energy infrastructure.

Demand response, distributed generation, distributed energy resources, smart grid, VPP, DPP, virtual power plant, AiGent, Voltus, CPower, GridBeyond, Enersponse, EnerNOC, Enel, FERC, energy storage, energy efficiency, data centers, emergency generator

America’s grid is under mounting strain.
PJM’s most recent capacity auction cleared at the price cap without enough capacity to meet demand, and data center load growth is outpacing new supply across every major market. AGent is unlocking a faster, smarter way to keep the power flowing: the backup generation that already sits at commercial, industrial, and mission-critical facilities, including AI data centers. AGent’s AI-based platform aggregates, orchestrates, and monetizes these assets, turning them into rapidly dispatchable, highly reliable distributed power plants. Because the equipment is already built, already paid for, and idle most of the year, AGent delivers capacity at the lowest cost of any new grid resource, at zero cost to the asset owner, who earns new revenue instead. AGent is already dispatching in three of the largest wholesale markets in North America, having successfully delivered capacity during grid emergency events in PJM, MISO, and ERCOT.
AGent will use the new capital to aggressively scale its team and accelerate its push to unlock 200+ GW of behind-the-meter generation across commercial and industrial facilities and the MUSH sector (municipalities, universities, schools, and hospitals), the properties with the highest concentration of on-site generation and the ones AGent’s team knows best.

“Twelve months ago, AGent was an idea backed by two investors who saw what we saw: 200+ GW of the most reliable generation in America sitting idle behind the meter,” said Stephanie Hendricks, CEO and Co-Founder of AGent. “Closing $17 million in our first year reflects both the urgency of the grid reliability challenge and the speed at which our team executes. With Spero, MassMutual Ventures, and Intrepid joining CIV and ZIP, we now have the partners and capital to bring this dispatchable capacity to the markets that need it most.”

“The grid doesn’t need to wait five years for new steel in the ground.
The capacity is already there, and AGent has built the intelligence layer to unlock it. Stephanie and her team have moved faster than any company we’ve seen in this space, and we’re proud to co-lead their Series Seed round,” said Stephen Wemple of Spero Ventures.

“When the grid is stressed, the difference between a rolling blackout and an ordinary afternoon is how fast dispatchable capacity shows up. AGent’s AI platform turns generation already sitting at hospitals, universities, and industrial sites into exactly that: capacity that responds in minutes, with no new construction and no cost to the owner. It’s a rare combination of climate resilience and hard economics, built by a team that has done this at scale before. That’s the sweet spot for our Climate Technology Fund: AI applied to real assets, with economics that pencil from day one,” said Aram Ouligian, Senior Associate at MassMutual Ventures.

# AGent Energy raises $11M to turn idle backup generators into grid capacity

● an hour ago

AGent Energy raises $11M to turn idle backup generators into grid capacity

**What's the deal?** [AGent Energy](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/aigent_energy) , a Houston-based startup that integrates backup generators into the grid during emergencies, raised $11 million in seed funding co-led by [Spero Ventures](https://app.dealroom.co/investors/spero_ventures) and [MassMutual Ventures](https://app.dealroom.co/investors/massmutual_ventures) . Intrepid Investment Management and existing investors [CIV](https://app.dealroom.co/investors/civ_2) and [Zero Infinity Partners](https://app.dealroom.
co/investors/zero_infinity_partners) joined the round, which ranks among the largest seed rounds ever for a US transportation and energy startup — above the 97th percentile.

**How it works:** The year-old company provides hardware and software that remotely switches on backup generators when grids face emergencies. That displaces demand at those sites, freeing up power for the rest of the grid. Its system works with diesel and gas generators and batteries.

**Why now?** Power demand is rising fast, straining grids and pushing up electricity bills, while new power plants remain slow and costly to build. AGent targets the generators that sit mostly idle at farms, hospitals, factories, big-box stores, and universities.

**What's the endgame?** AGent works with grid operators and utilities to supply extra capacity, sharing revenue with generator owners.
It already operates in three markets — Texas (ERCOT), the Midcontinent Independent System Operator region, and PJM — with a portfolio the size of a small power plant.

"This is the fastest and most capital-efficient way to add new capacity to the grid," said co-founder and chief executive officer Stephanie Hendricks, calling backup generation a "massive underutilized resource."

**By the numbers:** The startup has now raised $17 million in a year; CIV and Zero Infinity Partners provided $6 million previously. The Energy Department estimates more than 35 gigawatts of backup generation could respond to emergencies — enough, at one gigawatt per roughly 750,000 homes, to power millions — and AGent's estimate runs higher.

**What they're saying:** The Trump administration backs better use of existing assets.
"Leveraging backup generation as a last resort to mitigate power outages saves lives and reduces costs for American families," Deputy Energy Secretary James Danly said in a statement.

**The signal:** AGent is one of several companies tapping distributed resources like solar, batteries, and generators to support strained grids. "The grid doesn't need to wait five years for new steel in the ground," said Spero Ventures principal Stephen Wemple. "The capacity is already there, and AGent has built the intelligence layer to unlock it."
